solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Electrical device in vehicles, one not used earlier

indicators.note: one is left out of the vehicles, so the letter for one is dropped from that word

parts.note: trains are vehicles
one is the Roman numeral I
former means earlier

explanation.surface: Somebody describes a gadget inside cars, one that was never previously used.
explanation.definitionFit: A transformer is a device that changes the voltage of an alternating current.

clue.text: Sort of movement some solicitor set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read upwards, so the run is turned round
some of the word solicitor supplies a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A lawyer has arranged some sort of movement, perhaps a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary twitch, a kind of muscular movement.

clue.text: Needle and what it is (not the head)

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is cut off, the head being its start

parts.note: a needle is narrow, so this phrase gives the adjective narrow

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a needle and its own nature, minus its pointed end.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle on a dial or compass is a pointer, which is what an arrow is too.

clue.text: The writer enters bookshops maybe — to promote these?

definitions.text: The writer enters bookshops maybe — to promote these?

indicators.note: the writer goes into the shops, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bookshops are an example of stores
the writer refers to the setter, giving I

explanation.surface: An author visits bookshops to promote their tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: an author's tales are what they would promote in bookshops.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales and narratives are what a writer tours bookshops to sell.

clue.text: Protestants making sign going around province

indicators.note: the sign surrounds the province, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an omen is a sign
a province, as an area of activity, is a range

explanation.surface: Protestants marching with a banner through a province, Northern Ireland style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Province' suggests Ulster, but here it means sphere or scope.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangemen belong to the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternal body in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Theme of a thousand holy books — doubt

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
OT is the Old Testament, a set of holy books
an if is a doubt or condition, as in ifs and buts

explanation.surface: A sceptic's topic: a thousand scriptures, all in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or subject in a work, its theme.

clue.text: Page starts to rally some university bigwigs

parts.note: a recto is a right-hand page of a book

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A page boy kicks off a rally of senior academics.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectors head some universities, especially in Scotland, so they are senior figures.

clue.text: Note that is stupid!

definitions.meaning: the first note of the sol-fa scale
the exclamation made on realising something foolish

explanation.surface: Somebody spots a remark and exclaims at its foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sol-fa note and the cartoon cry of self-reproach popularised by Homer Simpson.

clue.text: Ruin of Roman camp, say

parts.note: Deva was the Roman fortress at what is now Chester
to say is to state

explanation.surface: A historian notes the ruins of an old Roman camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' reads as a noun about remains but is the verb. Chester is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To devastate is to wreck or lay waste, to ruin utterly.

clue.text: Heartless freethinker engages chaps joining English university about biblical interpretation

indicators.note: the shortened word takes in the other pieces, holding them inside
the middle letter of the word is removed, the heart being its centre

parts.note: a heretic thinks freely against orthodox belief
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted sceptic takes on English scholars over how to read scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the centre out of the freethinker word, and 'engages' says the shortened word wraps the chaps, English and university pieces; 'joining' just links those three.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermeneutic describes the theory and method of interpretation, especially of scripture.

clue.text: My roar, having bagged second bird

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces holds the other inside it, as in a bag

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!
to rant is to roar or rave
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a roar that has caught a second bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a large dark diving seabird.

clue.text: House where river meets bay

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: A dwelling at the point where a river runs into a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a verb here, to shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover is to shelter or protect, as you house something to keep it safe.

clue.text: Physicist has May meeting with top man

parts.note: may is the hawthorn, whose berry is the haw
a king is the top man

explanation.surface: A scientist has a meeting in May with the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month or a name but is the hawthorn tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Hawking was the celebrated British theoretical physicist.

clue.text: Reckless damage involving head of union to worry those folk reportedly

indicators.note: the damage word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: to harm is to damage

indicators.note: the first letter of union is taken
the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: to worry them is to scare 'em

explanation.surface: Careless damage to a union leader is meant to frighten people, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARE 'EM said casually gives the sound of SCARUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Harum-scarum means wild and impetuous, acting without thought of risk.

clue.text: Females primarily of dubious morality must include one?

definitions.text: Females primarily of dubious morality must include one?

indicators.note: primarily means only the opening letter of the word is used
the loose word has to hold the next piece inside it

parts.note: loose describes lax morals
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A prim question: should any account of women of doubtful virtue feature one?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a woman of loose morals is exactly what is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A floosie is a disapproving term for a woman seen as promiscuous.

clue.text: Fish sketches in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: roughs are rough drafts or sketches

explanation.surface: Drawings of fish on display in a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruff is a small European freshwater perch.

clue.text: Discernment shows gift horse to be phoney

indicators.note: being phoney means being fake, so the letters are a false arrangement

explanation.surface: Wisdom shows when a gift horse turns out to be a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to the proverb about not looking a gift horse in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the ability to see ahead, a form of perception and judgement.

clue.text: Drink made from extracts, something fishy

parts.note: to milk is to extract, as in milking a situation
a hake is a fish

explanation.surface: A beverage made from extracts that is somehow suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' looks like it means suspicious; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkshake is a cold drink of milk whipped with flavouring or ice cream.

clue.text: Behold, the fellow stuck in spring despaired

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: the fellow is put inside the spring word

parts.note: to start is to spring or jump
he refers to a man, the fellow

explanation.surface: Look, this chap was trapped in a spring and gave up hope.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to become discouraged, to give way to despair.

clue.text: People in business using charm sent all over the place

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Businesspeople spreading charm everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchants are traders, people who buy and sell goods.

clue.text: Latest bit of research on planet's hot locations?

indicators.note: the final letter of research is used

parts.note: the Earth is a planet, here with the possessive

explanation.surface: New research on the planet's hottest spots, as in global warming.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearths are fireplaces, the hot spots of a home; the question mark flags the playful definition.

clue.text: Crop beginning to wilt — feature of dry summer?

indicators.note: the opening letter of wilt is taken

parts.note: heat is a feature of a dry summer

explanation.surface: A crop starting to wilt in a hot, dry summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a cereal grown as a staple crop.

clue.text: Cowardly little devil gripped by desire

indicators.note: the little devil is held inside the desire word

parts.note: a wish is a desire
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: A timid imp in the grip of longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimpish means feeble and timid, lacking courage.

clue.text: Clown celebrity appearing in hoax

indicators.note: the celebrity shows up inside the hoax word

parts.note: cod means a hoax or sham, as in a cod accent
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous comedian is caught in a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard is the comic rustic in Shakespeare's Love's Labour's Lost.

clue.text: Put off detective writer, but not getting cross

indicators.note: the cross is left out, so its letter is removed

parts.note: Colin Dexter wrote the Inspector Morse detective novels
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Discouraging a crime novelist, who stays calm anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage, to put someone off acting.

clue.text: Grand residence, sumptuous hotel being demolished

parts.note: a home is a residence

indicators.note: the hotel is knocked down, so its letter goes

parts.note: rich means sumptuous
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grand house and a luxurious hotel are knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric means epic and heroic in scale, like the poems of Homer.

clue.text: Baddy, ruddy twisted inside

indicators.note: the interior letters are twisted round, changing places

parts.note: rouge is red, a ruddy colour

explanation.surface: A villain with a red face and a warped mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the U and G inside ROUGE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or villainous person.

clue.text: Solver's ending with nothing? Obtain source of synonyms

indicators.note: the end letter of solver's is used

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: A stuck solver asks where to find alternative words.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget's Thesaurus is the classic reference book of words with similar meanings.

clue.text: Individual drinkers may have this in joky manner

parts.note: tea is what drinkers may have
singly means one at a time, individually

explanation.surface: Solo drinkers might take this in a jokey way.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as TEA, SINGLY: what a lone drinker might have.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasingly means in a playful, mocking way.

clue.text: You may take a little time still

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Please take a moment and keep calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet means still, as in yet more or still to come.

clue.text: Something witty from mum? Not her!

indicators.note: not her means that word is dropped from the mum word

parts.note: mum is mother

explanation.surface: A child asks if mum made a joke, and is told it was someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A mot is a witty remark, as in bon mot.

clue.text: Most rough architects troubled about latest of designs

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the extra piece
troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred up
the final letter of designs is taken

explanation.surface: Architects are upset over their final, roughest plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' shuffles ARCHITECTS; 'about' wraps that around S, the last of designs.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratchiest means the roughest or most abrasive in texture.
